From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sudden latency spikes on hosted API since yesterday

Quick update from the runtime side: I see the canary swap for v2026-03-b happened yesterday 15:10 UTC (automated A/B canary, 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over ~3h). We're seeing an increase in mean KV cache eviction activity and an uptick in continuous-batching latencies for sequences around 512 tokens. Attached are initial logs (canary-logs-20260310.zip) and a perf diff I generated (perf-diff-clearline-20260310.csv).

Hypothesis: the new variant uses a slightly larger key-value cache footprint per request (different quantization/attention kernel path) that increases CPU-side serialization for small batches — this disproportionately affects small concurrent requests and drives p95/p99 up under existing batching heuristics.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll back canary to previous variant (v2026-03-a) — fast but loses behind-the-scenes improvements.
- Throttle the variant and reduce allowed batch size / increase batching concurrency to avoid serialization spikes.
- Quick patch to kernel selection to prefer a lower-latency attention kernel for short sequences (risky for throughput).

I'll keep digging and will post a narrow repro within 30m.

-rm
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Runtime Engineer
